newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela optimistic on Japan aluminum dispute.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela optimistic on Japan aluminum dispute.

text.p: A leading Venezuelan government official said on Tuesday he was optimistic a dispute with Japanese minority shareholders in aluminum smelter Venalum would be resolved through negotiations.
"It is only a question of time and talks before we reach a positive outcome," Elias Nadim Ynaty, president of state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) told reporters.

Ynaty, who returned recently from a talks with the Japanese consortium of Venalum shareholders in Tokyo, said the dispute over the Japanese shareholders' veto power would not need international arbitration.
Venezuelan officials failed to reach an agreement in Japan and accused Showa Denko KK of being inflexible.
Further talks about the 430,000 tonnes per year plant are scheduled to take place in Venezuela this month.
Venezuela hopes to sell controlling stakes in Venalum and three other aluminum companies by the end of the year.
Other members of the Japanese consortium include Kobe Steel Ltd, Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Mitsubishi Aluminum Co Ltd and Marubeni Corp.
